notes.title: New Freelancer: Su-Ren, The Robo-Roshi
notes.content:
[img]https://www.atlasreactorgame.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/10/blog_660x3001.jpg[/img]

Su-Ren will teach you the ways of duality.

[img]https://webcdn.triongames.com/ar/blog/suren/suren02.jpg[/img]

[h1]Basic Gameplay[/h1]
Su-Ren’s primary, Martial Master, is just the start of her “duality” theme. It has two targeter states – a medium ranged line or a shorter 360 degree AoE. Her healing ability, Serenity, is always useful, even if her allies aren’t within range because it also heals her. It’s a free action and synergizes incredibly well with her dash, Shifting Winds. Su-Ren’s dash targets an enemy or an ally, and then targets the opposite on the next turn – healing allies, damaging enemies! After dashing in, you can position yourself to body block for an ally, steal a buff, or even put more allies in range for your free action heal. Spirit Bend is great for when you’re just out of range with your other abilities, but still want to affect the fight. After targeting an ally or enemy – giving them might or weak respectively – any damage they do will spread the opposite status to their victims! This works great with targets that are about to use an AoE ability, as the reverse affect can spread to more targets.

[img]https://webcdn.triongames.com/ar/blog/suren/AltSkin.jpg[/img]

Karmic Justice, Su-Ren’s ultimate, is a massive shield that explodes on the following turn dealing a varying amount of damage based on how much damage the shield absorbed. She can save teammates on the brink of death, or ensure a massive AoE blast that’ll shred the opposing team’s health pool. Karmic Justice shines when you know a lot of damage will be focused on an ally. Knowing when to use her ult will be incredibly important to mastering Su-Ren!

[img]https://webcdn.triongames.com/ar/blog/suren/martialmaster.jpg[/img]

If Su-Ren doesn’t use Shifting Winds again on the turn after the first use of it, she won’t be able to dash again until it comes off cooldown. The probability of dashing twice in a row for maximum efficiency is something you can expect from Su-Ren. Consider countering this with traps, or not targeting her after her first dash, as she will most likely dash again. Most of her abilities are fairly short ranged, so displacements, roots, and slows can be very effective at keeping her out of the fight. When Karmic Justice comes up, predicting who she’ll shield is quite valuable – you don’t want to hit her shielded target because it’ll increase the damage it will do when it explodes on the following turn. Instead, take this chance to target another enemy. Su-Ren often needs to be in the middle of the fight to be effective, but has the tools to be evasive when needed. Take advantage of this predictable playstyle and maybe the student will become the teacher!

[img]https://webcdn.triongames.com/ar/blog/suren/karmicjustice.jpg[/img]

[h1]Abilities[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Martial Master[/b]
[list]
[*]Choose to either slam your staff down in a line, or sweep it around you.
[/list]
[*][b]Serenity[/b]
[list]
[*]As a free action, heal yourself and your allies in an area around you.
[/list]
[*][b]Shifting Winds[/b]
[list]
[*]Dash to an ally and heal them, or to an enemy to harm them. You may do this again on the following round, but to the opposite target.
[/list]
[*][b]Spirit Bend[/b]
[list]
[*]Grant an ally might, or a weaken a foe. The first time the target deals damage in the next 2 turns, it will spread the opposite affect on their targets.
[/list]
[*][b]Karmic Justice[/b]
[list]
[*]Give an ally a massive shield that will explode on the following turn, dealing damage based on how much damage it absorbed.
[/list]
[/list]

[img]https://webcdn.triongames.com/ar/blog/suren/serenity.jpg[/img]

[h1]Advanced Tactics[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]When playing as Su-Ren:[/b]
[list]
[*]Shifting Winds is essential for placing yourself in an ideal location to hit multiple allies with Serenity.
[*]Both forms of Martial Master have their uses. The circular attack is very useful if you think an enemy will dash near you.
[*]Aside from being a source of damage and healing, Shifting Winds mobility also allows for key body blocks and grabbing power-ups.
[*]When using Karmic Justice, consider placing it on an ally that has a dash up so they can place the explosion near as many enemies as possible.
[/list]

[*][b]Coming up against Su-Ren:[/b]
[list]
[*]The color of her Staff tells you who she can dash to. Green mean she has to dash to an ally, purple means she has to dash to an enemy.
[*]When dashing Su-Ren will always end up within two squares of her target, try to use traps or ground effects to punish her.
[*]She requires vision of her target in order to dash at them, stay in camo to avoid being targeted.
[*]When Su-Ren has max energy, she is likely to shield a low health ally. [*]Switch up targets when she is likely to shield an ally to diminish the effectiveness.
[list]
[/list]

notes.title: New Freelancer: Juno, The Last Word (Available 9/30/16)
notes.content:
[img]https://www.atlasreactorgame.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/09/juno_blog.jpg[/img]

Don’t cross Juno, The Last Word.

[h1]Basic Gameplay[/h1]
Juno’s primary, [b]Laser Barrage[/b], functions similarly to Celeste’s Strong Arm, but is an AoE and has unique pivots that allow her to hit some angles you might not otherwise have access to. When you’re absolutely sure an enemy is going to dash, use [b]Lockdown[/b] as a way to punish them! Knockbacks are incredibly powerful as they synergize well with traps and assist escapes, and on a 4 turn cooldown, you can employ [b]Off Limits[/b] to ensure your enemies are never where they want to be. Because of the way Juno’s ult works, she becomes a stationary target. Activating her [b]Riot Shield[/b] can give her the staying power she’ll need as the Head of OmniTrust Security.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/2cbcdfc954542d7a26f6a90fb42b30cfe226d6ed.png[/img]

Juno is the first freelancer to be able to use her ultimate, [b]Lay Down The Law[/b], before having earned max energy. For the low cost of 50 energy she hunkers down and combines the power from both of her laser cannons to create a solid beam that can stick around for multiple turns. Each turn the player has a choice to perform another ability and be able to move again, or pay 20 more energy to sweep the beam across a wide area. You can use this beam to cut off escapes or just de-atomize those stubborn enough to stick around.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/f9652c8cd1b6aa4ff8004a8f1b91da8cb45581cb.jpg[/img]

Juno is still a Firepower, even with 140 hp and a 40 point shield on a 3 turn cooldown. Enemies will take advantage of those turns you don’t have your Riot Shield available, and even more so when you’ve rooted yourself to perform your ultimate. Always try to take cover and, if possible, time your Riot Shield to use during your ultimate. Enemies will also use your rooted ultimate as the perfect time to just walk away from you. Work with your team to corner them, root or slow them, and keep them in your sights. If they get behind you during your ultimate, you’re in bad shape because you can only sweep your beam so far!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/0f3486f4703356d326b53ca39334f20938d9d461.jpg[/img]

[h1]Abilities[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Laser Barrage[/b]
[list]
Sweep each laser cannon along their own areas. Crossing them deals even more damage.
[/list]
[*][b]Lockdown[/b]
[list]
Tether an enemy and punish them for moving too far.
[/list]
[*][b]Off Limits[/b]
[list]
Smash your laser cannons down creating a shock wave that knocks enemies back.
[/list]
[*][b]Riot Shield[/b]
[list]
Activate a free action shield that takes the edge off enemy attacks.
[/list]
[*][b]Lay Down The Law[/b]
[list]
Anchor yourself down and fire off a continuous laser beam that also deals damage if passed through. On following turns, use more energy to sweep it across the battlefield.
[/list]
[/list]

[h1]Advanced Tactics[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]When playing as Juno:[/b]
[list]
[*]Juno’s Laser Barrage covers a lot of ground. Even if you can’t see your enemies you can still potentially hit them by firing into camo.
[*]Lockdown is a great tool against dashes. Use it on likely targets such as low health freelancers that have a dash available.
[*]Off Limits is useful for creating space – wait for enemy frontliners to engage then push them back.
[*]Even though you can use your ultimate at 50 energy, consider holding onto it longer so you can sweep it multiple turns.
[*]Be aware of your weaknesses – no dash and a stationary ult can leave you stranded behind your team or away from the fight if you’re not careful.
[/list]

[*][b]Coming up against Juno:[/b]
[list]
[*]Counter Juno’s ultimate by forcing her to take large amounts of damage with persistent damage fields and big damage delayed effects such as Zuki’s Big One.
[*]Burst Juno down when her shield is on cooldown.
[*]Juno can dish out tons of damage but can’t fire over walls, avoid straying into her line of fire by keeping out of line of sight and hitting her from afar. Getting behind her when she ults forces her to consider ending her ult early.
[*]As a frontliner try to have a source of unstoppable when engaging with Juno to mitigate the effects of Off Limits.
[/list]
[/list]

Join the community on Discord! https://discord.gg/0KC8Z8wyQHjiWofk

[h1]Open Beta Hotfix[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue where sometimes it would appear like a freelancer was in a [*]position that they were not actual in (this also fixes an issue where it could appear like 2 freelancers were on the same square)
[*]Fixed an issue causing catalyst abilities to still be shown during Decision [*]Phase as if an actor were using them, even though they were already queued/used on a prior turn.
[*]Fixed an issue where Oz could move incorrectly after using Made You Look
[*]Fixed an exception caused when entering Spectator Mode in custom games
[*]Fixed the chapter 4 mission, "Complete 5 different daily missions." to correctly increment upon daily completion.
[*]Fixed an exception caused when closing the progression screen with Fill selected
[*]Fixed an issue where recently used chat would not disappear at the wrong time
[*]Fixed an issue where chat input could turn all white
[*]Fixed (hopefully) the Entry Text tooltip bug. We really love this bug -_-
[/list]

[h1]Open Beta has started![/h1]
[list]
[*]Atlas Reactor is now in Open Beta!
[*]Everyone will have full access during the Open Beta period
[*]Purchase the game for full access when Headstart begins on 9/30!
[/list]

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
[list]
[*]Respawn beacons are no longer affected by camouflage.
[*]Oz can now select a move after using Made You Look
[*]Orion - Fate Transfer - Energy Leech mod now correctly increases the incoming energy through damage transferred by 25% to a total of 125%.
[/list]

[h1]Advanced Pings[/h1]
[list]
[*]Advanced Pings - While holding down alt, click and hold the mouse button down. After 0.25 seconds, an advanced ping menu will appear! Choose your advanced ping type by hovering over the type you want and then releasing the mouse button (or stay over the X in the center to cancel).
[/list]

[h1]Fill[/h1]
[list]
[*]There is now a “Fill” option in Freelancer Select
[*]This will allow you to choose your Freelancer after getting paired with your team, so you can choose a role that best compliments your team comp
[*]As probably expected, you will not be able to select a Freelancer that one of your teammates already has
[*]Currently only one member in a group can choose the Fill option. We are looking into changing this.
[/list]

[h1]Clash[/h1]
[list]
[*]The Clash system has been implemented to resolve a very specific case where two players are equidistant from a location and both choose to move to that same location
[*]Previously the player that locked in first would get to the square, with the other player getting bumped off of it, but this was “hidden” information and it was not clear to players how the winner was determined.
[*]Now, with Clash, both players are bumped off of the target location to an adjacent square
[list]
[*]If there is a powerup on the target square, neither player will get that powerup if they clash
[*]If players are equidistant from a square and they are both walking through it, they will also clash and neither will get the powerup
[*]If a player finishes on that location while another player walks through it, the player that finishes on that location will get the powerup
[/list]
[*]This system allows players to plan around this known mechanic and not have to guess on who clicked first. It is part of our larger goal to not hide information from the player and provide a clear set of rules with which to make decisions
[*]The Clash system also applies to evades
[/list]

[h1]UI[/h1]
[list]
[*]There is now a simpler way to choose AI bot difficulty, with choices of Easy/Medium/Hard. You can toggle back to the old start interface if desired
[*]Added more animations to the in-match HUD to make it clear when abilities are placed and canceled
[*]The cursor will now notify you of how many clicks are required to fully place an ability
[/list]

[h1]Orion Skin[/h1]
[list]
[*]Orion’s new Colossus skin is now in game!
[/list]

[h1]General[/h1]
[list]
[*]Completing a tier in the faction system now results in a system broadcast letting everyone know it has been completed.
[*]The 3d model for the 5th character on your team is now visible (in 16:9 at least) when making custom games with 5 players on a team. Make sure you're all color coordinated! ;-)
[*]Players that have temporary full access are now notified that they are in this state
[*]Many Particle effects now have distortion effects on them
[*]Particle effects will not have a distortion effect when Graphics Quality is set to Low. This increases free memory and, in some circumstances, frame rate.
[*]Various minor bug fixes
[/list]

[h1]Progression Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*]We have dramatically increased the experience (xp) rewards from mission and challenges, and made corresponding reductions from "bonus" xp sources. This was done to grant more satisfying rewards for completing content, and to wrangle the incredible high variance of the GG boost bonus. [*]Additionally, we have slightly reduced the pace of early Season and Freelancer levels to smooth out the reward rate for new users. However, we have also reduced the time to level Freelancers at the top end.
[/list]

[h1]Freelancer Levels[/h1]
[list]
[*]The amount of xp required to gain levels after Freelancer Level 20 has been reduced from 50,000 to 30,000.
[*]Mod Tokens are now awarded at Freelancer levels 4/8/12 instead of 5/10/15. These are given in packs of 6. Up from 5.
[/list]

[h1]Mission Rewards[/h1]
[list]
[*]Daily Mission xp rewards have been doubled, increased from 500-1000 to 1000-2000.
[*]Chapter Missions now award 3000, 4000, or 5000 xp depending on difficulty.
[*]The Chapter 5 Challenge is repeatable. After earning the title, you can complete the Ultimate Challenge again for an xp reward.
[/list]

[h1]Bonuses[/h1]
[list]
[*]Playing with Friends bonus decreased from 50% to 25%.
[*]Bonuses from GG boosts have been reduced. The total xp bonus from GG boosts is now 100%.
[*]Using a GG boost grants a 30% xp bonus to yourself, and a 10% xp bonus to everyone else in the match.
[*]Don't despair -- we all love passive bonuses, but GG boosts are destined for greater things this coming Season!
[*]We will continue to play and adjust these bonuses as necessary.
[/list]

[h1]Season Changes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Chapter 5 has been created for Open Beta. You'll be able to experience the true chapter stories and the conclusion of the Trust War starting October 4!
[*]Chapters now contain 5 missions each.
[*]Only 4 out of the 5 missions must be completed to progress to the next chapter.
[/list]

[h1]Season Levels[/h1]
[list]
[*]We have removed some of the rewards from early Season Levels. These will reappear in a different location at launch.
[/list]

notes.title: New Freelancer: Orion, The Empyrean (available 8/30/2016)
notes.content:
[img]https://www.atlasreactorgame.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/08/blog_660x3001.jpg[/img]
[i]Bow down before Orion, The Empyrean.[/i]

Orion will bear your burden… and grow [b]stronger[/b] for it!
[img]https://webcdn.triongames.com/ar/blog/orion/stats.jpg[/img]

[b]BASIC GAMEPLAY[/b]
Orion is very unique support. He doesn’t naturally gain energy based on using his abilities, though they can be modded to do so. He’s got a passive similar to Rask where he gains energy every time he takes damage. For every 20 energy he holds, he gains 1 shard. These shards empower his other abilities but are only consumed when he uses his ult or dies (He’ll maintain 25% of his energy when he dies, which is 1 shard!).

[img]https://webcdn.triongames.com/ar/blog/orion/floating_01.jpg[/img]

Orion’s primary, Empyreal Ruin, is great for raining down some AoE damage that ignores cover, and the area grows larger the more shards you’ve gained. His Fate Transfer uses his own life to protect an ally by taking 75% of the damage they would take. Luckily it also provides a shard empowered shield to protect his own life and is a solid way for him to gain energy. Orion can place a Quantum Core on an ally that explodes when they take damage. It’s a free action ability that has versatile mods. Astral Infusion heals himself or an ally over 2 turns and is increasingly effective with more shards. Orion’s ultimate is unusual because he actually loves holding at 100 energy as it makes most of his abilities stronger! But if you’re going to die you’ll lose 75% of your energy anyway, so you might as well drop the Cosmic Flare, healing yourself and damaging enemies in a large radius. Sure, you’ll consume your energy, but if you live, you get another chance to build it back up again to protect your team and rain down some destruction in the process.

[img]https://webcdn.triongames.com/ar/blog/orion/floating_02.jpg[/img]

Orion’s ability to take damage for his allies is dramatically reduced if he’s got less health. Often times he’ll have to heal himself instead of an ally to be able to continue doing his job, so positioning in cover and not being focused is a very important goal. You’ll find your best chance to get rid of him if you can force him to decide between protecting himself or his ally. If you’re up against an Orion, be sure to protect and even steal those Energize buffs. Giving him energy really just does make him stronger.

[b]ABILITIES[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Empyreal Ruin[/b]
[list]
[*]Rains down a blast of empyrean energy in an area that grows with more shards.
[/list]
[*][b]Fate Transfer[/b]
[list]
[*]Redirect most of the damage dealt to an ally and mitigate it by shielding yourself.
[/list]
[*][b]Quantum Core[/b]
[list]
[*]Focus pure energy around an ally that erupts when dealt damage.
[/list]
[*][b]Astral Fusion[/b]
[list]
[*]Regenerate the health of an ally for 2 turns, sharing the first turn, or heal yourself for both turns.
[/list]
[*][b]Cosmic Flare[/b]
[list]
[*]Consume 5 shards to unleash a large area blast against enemies that also heals himself.
[/list]
[/list]

[b]ADVANCED TACTICS[/b]

[b]When playing as Orion:[/b]
[list]
[*]Generating energy is incredibly important to achieving peak power levels.
[*]Make sure to use Fate Transfer on an ally you are sure will be hit, especially when you are at low energy levels.
[*]Astral Fusion is most effective when used on allies as it will heal you as well, but it can be used for self-survivability at the cost of efficiency.
[*]Choose battles wisely — playing too conservatively will leave you weak but too aggressively can lead to an early grave.
If you need power above all else consider walking through hazards to generate energy.
[*]Cosmic Flare is a powerful ability but when used consumes your shards. [*]Good Orion players ride the line between staying at maximum power and detonating their ultimate at the right moment.
[/list]

[b]Coming up against Orion:[/b]
[list]
[*]When you think Orion will use his Fate Transfer available try to guess his most likely target and then attack someone else or him directly.
[*]Area of effect abilities are potentially a good counter to Fate Transfer. He will take the damage of two targets if you hit both him and his Fate Transfer recipient.
[*]Focus on Orion when he is at max energy — he can’t get any stronger and killing him causes him to lose most of his energy. If he is forced to use [*]Cosmic Flare all of his other abilities become weaker.
[*]Ignore him as much as possible while he is at low energy so he stays that way. Orion generates almost all of his energy when hit by abilities. Sometimes you may want to avoid hitting him with an area of effect skill so he doesn’t become stronger.
[/list]

notes.title: New Freelancer: Blackburn, The Last Soldier (available 7/12/2016)
notes.content:
[h1]Meet Blackburn, The Last Soldier.[/h1]
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/0de06b7b82de155a5d7f75339108c728fe80fd30.jpg[/img]

Blackburn will tactically sow the seeds of destruction among the enemy team.

[u][b]Basic Gameplay[/b][/u]
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/8d54ff52ee5cd53026fb3268c0015a5db91b84e3.jpg[/img]

Blackburn’s primary, Equalizer, is made to be versatile for every situation; You can put down one target or chip away with the AoE setting. When you’re stuck behind a wall, just have Blackburn toss over his Proteus Grenade. Enemies are rarely out of reach for him. In the case you find yourself out of range, pop your Adrenal Stim to help you pick up your step and dole out the damage. It’s also a free action, so always be ready to see him with Might! He’s an experienced soldier that knows to keep his back to the wall. His Blitz always puts him next to cover and lays down suppressing fire during the blast phase. You can’t just be worried about Blackburn on the ground, because he’s got some pretty hefty backup flying in the skies above. He can call down strafing fire that’ll wreck all enemy’s silly enough to make the mistake of lining up for him.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/eb6952243f28e6600f6012100168a62d337c81d8.jpg[/img]

Blackburn’s tactical prowess makes him hard to play against, but there are ways to counterplay his positioning. He’s only able to dash to cover, which makes his destinations somewhat predictable. Plan your shots accordingly, and definitely punish him after he’s Blitzed. Grouping against Blackburn is basically a death sentence because his toolkit provides plenty of ways to punish cuddle puddles. Keeping him off the battlefield as much as possible is another way to ensure he isn’t constantly dishing out the damage. Learning when and how to focus him down may just mean you get to live to see another round!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/38d2c574fdee6261acc825b9b2c3bbb50743bd4a.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Abilities[/b][/u]

[b]Equalizer[/b]
Attacks either a single target with high damage or a group of enemies with lower damage based on targeting.

[b]Proteus Grenade[/b]
Throws a grenade dealing area of effect damage. It can go over walls, and even be modded to heal.

[b]Adrenal Stim[/b]
Inject yourself with a free action stim that grants haste and might until the end of the turn.

[b]Blitz[/b]
Dash to cover and then choose a direction to set up overwatch, damaging enemies in a cone during blast phase.

[b]Scorched Earth[/b]
Call in an air strike to deal massive damage to enemies in a line.

[u][b]Advanced Tactics[/b][/u]

[b]When playing as Blackburn:[/b]
[list]
[*]Use the “wide fire” mode on Equalizer to cover locations your enemies may dash to.
[*]Keep a wall between you and your target on the turn Proteus Grenade is available. You can deal damage while potentially not taking any.
[*]Stay near cover as much as possible when you move so that you can dash into an advantageous position with Blitz.
[*]Blitz is a dash ability that fires in blast. Use it to evade enemies’ dash abilities and then damage them in return.
[*]Blackburn works well with characters who reveal: Blitz, Proteus Grenade, and Scorched Earth can easily finish off targets that escape around walls.
[/list]

[b]Coming up against Blackburn:[/b]
[list]
[*]Scorched Earth hits all his targets in a line across the entire battlefield. [*]Avoid grouping up when Blackburn is at full energy.
[*]Blackburn’s dash is on a five turn cooldown and he can only move a short distance. Focus him down after he uses Blitz.
[*]Blackburn is stronger when he’s next to cover. Try to push or pull him out of covered areas while fighting him.
[*]Just because Blackburn is behind a wall don’t assume you are safe. Many of his attacks have ways to circumvent barriers.
[/list]

notes.title: Last Chance to Earn Beta Elo Emblems!
notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/61274db452f8f9088083482c1e002e6ac9771fa0.jpg[/img]

Hey Lancers,It’s me, Muzzy, your friendly neighborhood Gremolitions chump. I’m here to talk about the wipe on the horizon!

I know, I know. You saw the word “wipe” and your separation anxiety is kicking in. Mine did too. Let’s all take a deep breath, knock back a can of Rask’s Brain Juice, put on our honorary game developer’s pants and look at what this means for the health of the game.

First of all, we are one patch closer to release! Were excited that we’re making progress. Secondly, this is a limited wipe. We’ve taken care to only reset areas that we need for testing, while leaving other area of progression untouched. We want to affect your experience as little as possible while also getting proper testing done. Wipes are essential for progressing the game experience. Devs need to know how a new feature functions from a fresh starting line, rather than in the middle of a race. We are, after all, in the wonderful world of Beta, where pay models change, lancers are OP, and we’ve had to swallow more bugs than a contestant on Fear Factor.

[b]Important Notice:[/b] This is the last weekend to get the Freelancer Elo Beta Emblems! We will be introducing new Emblems to achieve in the next patch.


I’ll walk you through what’s going to be reset:
[u]Season Progress[/u]
[list]
[*]Because of your extraordinary playtesting, we’ve learned a lot! With this wipe, we’ll apply the lessons we’ve learned and give players a more consistent and fluid Season progression in a way that solves some of the issues we’ve identified. We’ll also give players an additional chapter to unlock! We are very interested in your feedback on other changes to the Seasons system as well. We’ll be beginning at Chapter 1 again, to test progress, but you’ll notice the unlock on subsequent chapters will be accelerated.
[/list]
[u]Season Rewards[/u]
[list]
[*]It wouldn’t make much sense to wipe the Season progression without wiping the reason you progress! I’m going to miss a couple of the styles for my favorite lancers, and especially the emoticons. However, since the experience is being tweaked, I’m excited to earn, craft, and open those Loot Matrices again – it’s like Christmas every level!
[/list]
[u]Purchased Items[/u]
[list]
[*]All your credits will be restored and any items you had obtained directly or indirectly via those purchases will be wiped.
[/list]

What we are NOT wiping:
[list]
[*]You will not lose your Freelancer levels.
[*]Any awards you’ve earned, like Elo Banners and that elusive “Killed By Dev” title will stick around. (And yes, these are just examples, not the full list. “Dev Killer”, “Catalyzer”, etc will also not be wiped)
[*]Non-Season player experience will not be wiped. You will still have level 10 which gives you access to Seasons. If you are not level 10 yet, you will maintain your current level.
[*]Both Freelancer Elo and Player Elo will not be wiped.
[/list]

This partial wipe is no easy task. The Devs explained to me just how much easier it is to do a full wipe/reset rather than this partial one, but they’re willing to put in the extra work as a service to the players while still wiping the minimum needed to carry the forward-thinking vision that game development requires.


[b]IMPORTANT:[/b] It’s Beta. This is not the last wipe.

We have some time before we launch and that time will be filled with tons of development and polish. Much as with Seasons, we will be introducing other features that will give us all the best experience if started with a clean slate.
Beta is about experiencing a game before it releases, growing with the community and the game. In order to do so, there are certain aspects of Alpha/Beta events that we have to set our expectations properly to deal with. Be prepared!

Because of all our dedicated players, we have already gained a massive amount of data and feedback to help us create a much better user experience. I thank you, the team thanks you, and all of the players that will ever play this game are indebted to you for the time, dedication and patience you’ve extended to us.

– The Atlas Reactor Team

notes.title: New Freelancer: Celeste
notes.content:
Meet Celeste, The Rogue.
[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/7b04fb369671b1bb39c4a4bac6e58afc7586211a.jpg[/img]

Celeste will steal your heart, or at least any valuables you may have.

[u][b]Basic Gameplay[/b][/u]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/5d03fb452f894d007b49072b1f6bc8a6d7947942.jpg[/img]

Celeste’s primary, Strong Arm, functions similarly to Grey’s Tranquilizer Dart – mouse closer = split more – and has the ability to pickup the spoils from afar – Haste, Energize, Might, and Heal! If you’re good at predictions, her Proximo Charge is a good tool to lay down some surprise damage and it’s quite effective at booby trapping the spoils you decide not to steal. Celeste’s Smoke Bombs ability is the first of it’s kind; it affects your enemy’s vision. We can’t wait to see the way you use this to your tactical advantage. Her dash, On The Run, allows Celeste to escape around corners and deal damage along the way. There’s even a mod for it that helps you lose your would be pursuers by dashing through your Smoke Bombs to turn invisible! Celeste’s ultimate, Safecracker, is a very powerful version of her primary that can gain the same buffs that her targets have – Energize, Might, Haste!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/5356cf7512a14bbbf6c49808b9d3c625c6c4fb59.jpg[/img]

As with any kit with a free action ability you may feel stuck without options while your abilities come off cooldown. Lucky for you, her primary is really fun and effective. Being a Firepower, she’s quite squishy, and because she uses line of sight for all of her abilities, she tends to have to be in unfavorable places. You can counteract this by trying to stay in cover and using the range on her primary to your advantage. Like all master thieves, the shadows are your friend. The element of surprise may be your best bet in winning trades.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/e8a08bf5790972960957e68e91eddf89b8d55e01.jpg[/img]

[u][b]Abilities[/b][/u]

[b]Strong Arm[/b]
Launch two grapplers, which can deal damage to two separate targets or heavier damage to a single target. Grapplers can also can target power-ups instead, for use on the next turn.

[b]Promximo Charge[/b]
Place a 4-turn trap that is invisible to enemies. If the enemy is on the trap during Blast Phase, the trap explodes, dealing direct damage. The trap takes 1 turn to arm and cannot detonate the turn it’s placed.

[b]Smoke Bombs[/b]
Throw two smoke bombs that last until the end of the next turn. Smoke bombs block line of sight and deal indirect damage per turn.

[b]On The Run[/b]
Dash to two locations in quick succession. Enemies hit take direct damage.

[b]Safecracker[/b]
Fire dual grapplers that pass through enemies, targeted just like Strong Arm. If enemies hit have active might, energize, or haste buffs, gain the same effect the next turn.

[u][b]Advanced Tactics[/b][/u]

[b]When playing as Celeste:[/b]
[list]
[*]Position yourself so that you have clear line of sight to powerups. Grabbing them when you don’t have enemies within line of sight is a good way to keep an edge without having to stray too far from the action.
[*]Be mindful of where enemies are in relation to Smoke Bombs, good placement means that you can see your enemies while they can’t see you.
[*]On The Run can be useful for getting around corners and positioning yourself onto power-ups appearing next turn.
[*]Place Proximo mines on locations you know enemies will want to end their turn such as on power-ups or behind common cover locations.
[*]Safecracker can do immense damage but requires good positioning, try to catch enemies unawares by using Smoke Bombs.
[/list]

[b]Coming up against Celeste:[/b]
[list]
[*]Celeste is very good at grabbing power-ups before you can move to them. [*]Consider dashing to them or moving to them the turn before they appear.
[*]Move through Smoke Bombs after they are placed to get vision for your allies.
[*]Be mindful of what area Celeste is in when she places her Proximo mine and try to avoid that zone.
[*]Spread out when she has her ultimate ability, it can be devastating to grouped up targets.
[/list]

notes.title: New Freelancer: Dr. Finn
notes.content:
Meet Dr. Finn, The ‘Eeler.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/446ef809f1f1980bb7298a3ee1b19821164ff34b.jpg[/img]

Dr. Finn is an ef[b]fish[/b]ient support who’s not afraid to fight!

[u][b]Basic Gameplay[/b][/u]

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/30ba0d064af488a3ed5d196453ded210bcc4e70d.jpg[/img]

Dr. Finn is a Support lancer with healing, protection, disruption, and his primary attack is actually quite potent. He is very good at causing the enemy team to spread out, and with his ult, he can even cause them to clump together. His primary, Water Spout, is a large, adjustable AoE cone; Wider = less damage, Narrow = more damage. Refreshing Spray is great for full team heals given it’s large AoE cone, and it even heals Dr. Finn a little too! Electrifying eel does a great job of punishing enemies that clump because it jumps from enemy to enemy. Dr. Finn’s Bubble Trouble create a great opportunity to protect squishy allies with a shield, followed up by a good sized AoE slow once it pops. When you’ve got 100 energy Maelstrom is a great tool to line up amazing combos by pulling all enemies within it’s large radius towards the center of it.

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/24758151/2b3e8693d77bfe1785d04c1c544e64349557c101.jpg[/img]

His most prominent weakness is his lack of dashes, but between Bubble Trouble’s solid shielding and slow combo, and Refreshing Spray’s self healing, he can tank a surprising amount of damage. When they realize chasing you isn’t netting a kill fast enough, they’ll change targets to your allies. Your wide, long cone has the coverage to put pressure on them as they run away. And when they manage to jump on your allies after giving up on you, your Maelstrom provides great way to peel them off your team! A true support, through and through.

You can check out his Taunts and Abilities here:

[u][b]Abilities[/b][/u]

[b]Water Spout[/b] 
     Dr. Finn fires off a high pressure water stream in a cone that deals more damage the more narrow the player makes it.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YalaA6WDl2w&list=PL_p7iQgAOdKWiJiV_taZMb3g4mtYR2aO3&index=2

[b]Refreshing Spray[/b]
     Dr. Finn sends healing bubbles out in a large cone that also heals himself a little.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K7zO1LufHuU&list=PL_p7iQgAOdKWiJiV_taZMb3g4mtYR2aO3&index=4

[b]Electrifying Eel[/b]
     Dr. Finn launches an electrified eel at an enemy lancer, dealing damage. The eel jumps to a nearby enemy next blast phase dealing damage again.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=THjQh6NW-5c&list=PL_p7iQgAOdKWiJiV_taZMb3g4mtYR2aO3&index=6

[b]Bubble Trouble[/b]
     Dr. Finn protects an ally (or himself) with a bubble shield during Prep and pops during Blast, dealing damage and slowing nearby enemies.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5yvv3mACKSQ&list=PL_p7iQgAOdKWiJiV_taZMb3g4mtYR2aO3&index=8

[b]Maelstrom[/b]
     Dr. Finn creates a maelstrom of churning waters that deals damage and pulls enemies towards it’s center.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=grYIRTo6dM4&list=PL_p7iQgAOdKWiJiV_taZMb3g4mtYR2aO3&index=10

[u][b]Advanced Tactics[/b][/u]

[b]When playing as Dr. Finn:[/b]

[list]
[*]Position yourself so that Refreshing Spray can hit multiple allies. Works well with melee ‘lancers that group together
[*]Many of Finn’s abilities are blocked by walls, be conscious of where you end your turn so that you keep line of sight to your desired targets. If you need to position defensively make sure Bubble Trouble is off cooldown so you can still help your team since its targeting is unaffected by line of sight.
[*]Finn can generate immense amounts of energy by hitting large groups of people. Consider using Water Spout over other cooldowns to build up an early ultimate.
[*]While Finn doesn’t have a dash, Bubble Trouble is excellent for disengaging against melee lancers with its defensive capabilities.
[*]Maelstrom has high potential for wombo combos. Try pairing with another lancer that can take advantage of the large AoE pull in.
[*]Placing Bubble Trouble on a Frontliner dashing in is a good way to keep enemies grouped up due to the slow.
[/list]

[b]Coming up against Dr. Finn:[/b]
[list]
[*]Stay spread out if possible, all of Finn’s abilities hit multiple targets
[*]Focus Finn when his Bubble Trouble is on cooldown. He has poor self preservation without the bubble.
[*]The eels jump to ‘lancers within 5 spaces. If you have eels on you consider dashing away from your team before they can jump or if your friend is eeled dash away from them if you don’t want to take the damage.
[*]Use displacement to try and get Finn or his allies behind walls so that he can’t get full value out of his AoE heal.
[/list]
